column1: > Source-reference records for the files named by installer/payload.tsv.
> installer/validate.py checks their shape. The final release checks the
> optional provider refs below against prepared/published public commits;
> redist/tools.tsv separately selects exact executable module versions.
> id      the name payload.tsv uses
> repo    owner/name on github.com, or "-" for the repository being built
> ref     a full 40-hex commit, because a branch is not a pin, or "-" while
>         the exact release source remains unselected. A "-" ref is loud:
>         validate.py prints the source as unpinned, and --src takes the
>         checkout it is handed. A --bin build may take a separately qualified
>         prebuilt executable regardless of this ref. The 0.4 release gate
>         requires exact source commits for localstores, modelhost,
>         lemonadeimage, thenoiseimage, pytorchimage and pytorchengine before
>         publishing its final package candidate.
> UNRESOLVED is a source with no verified published commit. A payload row naming
> it must be gated by a preprocessor variable in abstraction.wxs, and the
> workflow leaves it out of the package and says so in the job summary. It is not
> a placeholder to be filled in silently: somebody has to decide where that file
> is published from and verify its commit.
> localstores is abstraction-storage-over-local-stores, whose
> go/cmd/inventoryd is an optional provider feature. The split manifest and
> published.tsv already name that public repository. Its row remains "-"
> until the final 0.4 candidate pins its exact source; redist/tools.tsv
> supplies the separately qualified prebuilt executable to a --bin package.
> panel is the control panel, published into openabstractions/abstractions as the
> module github.com/openabstractions/abstractions/monitor. The directory reaches
> that repository through scripts/split.manifest's "tree monitor monitor"; the
> tag a module in a subdirectory takes is monitor/vX.Y.Z. The release route
> builds its Panel executable from the module version in redist/tools.tsv.
> The panel and charter refs here retain historical source-reference commits;
> they do not select the final candidate's executable bytes or module versions.
> modelhost is abstraction-provider-modelhost, whose go/cmd/modelhostd is
> another optional provider feature. The split manifest and published.tsv
> already name that public repository. Its row remains "-" until the final
> 0.4 candidate pins its exact source; redist/tools.tsv supplies the
> separately qualified prebuilt executable to a --bin package.
> modelhostengine is the reviewed upstream llama.cpp b10825 Windows x64 Vulkan
> release asset. The source commit identifies its publisher's build; the
> archive's exact SHA-256 and every kept file are checked before the reduced
> 24-file OA bundle is derived. Only that separately pinned bundle enters the
> x64 MSI. Windows ARM64 retains the provider but has no reviewed bundle.
> lemonadeimage is abstraction-provider-lemonade. The release tools roster
> selects its planned go/v0.4.0 module for lemonaded.exe. The Windows x64
> --bin route includes the executable and its declaration when the qualified
> binary is supplied. The pin below identifies its exact prepared public
> source; binary qualification remains separate. The engine and model are
> separate Setup effects with their own consent and pins.
> pytorchimage and pytorchengine both name the same prepared
> abstraction-provider-pytorch source commit. The first builds pytorchd; the
> second is a prepared local-input directory, whose existing enginefiles
> manifest comes from that same-source pytorchd setup inputs command. Its
> CPython, lock-selected wheels and Hummingbird byte pins and license notices
> remain owned by the provider. This source reference does not qualify those
> native inputs or claim that Go built the third-party binaries. Genuine CI
> input provenance and the final measured bundle identity remain release holds.
> ipclibrary is the abstraction-identity commit the abstraction-ipc wheel is
> built from (research/org-edits/redist/pypi.tsv). Its directory is the one file
> the release workflow takes out of that run's win_amd64 wheel,
> abstraction/ipc/_native/abstraction_ipc.dll; a workstation passes a folder
> holding a built abstraction_ipc.dll as --src ipclibrary=DIR.
